svg.title: Negotiation, concessions and rights exchange: selected milestones and original sources
svg.text: Negotiation, concessions & rights exchange
Selected milestones in Cleuson, Gougra, Hongrin-Léman and Valais irrigation
Chronological sequence; spacing is not proportional. Date ranges are placed by their outcome.
Documented event
Model terms
Future expiry / obligation
Superscripts → source notes
Late 1800s /
Navizence · Initial concession grants
Ayer (late 1800s) + St-Jean (1902) → private holders: water-power concessions.
Volumes / payments: not specified.
Granges · An early agreement
Granges consortium ↔ Chippis-Sierre power station: first agreement.
Rights transferred / quantities / payments: not specified for the 1902 agreement.
Lower Navizence · A 99-year concession
Seven municipalities → AIAG: Vissoie–Chippis water-power concession, 99 years.
Volumes / payments: not specified.
Navizence · Two concessions transferred
Private concession holders → Sierre industrial services (SIS): 2 concessions.
Transfer price / water volumes: not specified.
Lower Printse · Initial concession grant
Nendaz → a private holder: water-power use between Beuson and Aproz.
Later holder → Lonza: subsequent transfer; date / price not specified.
Briey · Notarized irrigation entitlement
Notarial deed → Briey irrigation: 120 L/s, 1 June–31 August each year.
Entitlement documented; a transfer between holders is not established.
Stalden · Municipal purchase of a bisse
Previous holders → Stalden municipality: irrigation-channel asset (recollection).
Municipality → seller(s): purchase price not specified; water-right scope unclear.
Gougra · Grants followed by an undated transfer
Grimentz + Ayer → 2 private holders: Gougra water-power concessions.
Private holders → Isotherme SA: later transfer; year / price not specified.
The later transfer cannot be dated to before 1950 from this passage.
Haute-Printse · Concession to EOS
Nendaz → EOS: Haute-Printse and tributary water-power concession.
Volumes / payments: not specified; existing irrigation supply is reserved.
Cleuson · Rights for electricity
Bornet estate → EOS: rights (quantity not specified).
EOS → Bornet estate: electricity (kWh not specified).
Gougra · Concessions transferred before dam construction
Isotherme SA → FMG: its various water-power concessions.
Transfer price / water volumes: not specified.
Saxon · Substitute water supply
FMM → Saxon: substitute supply for an existing 350 L/s entitlement.
EOS → FMM: compensation (amount not specified).
Hongrin · Shared concession authority
Vaud + Fribourg → FMHL: joint hydropower concession (1963).
FMHL → cantons: financial terms not specified in this passage.
Bouillets · Water-source access and cost repayment
Nendaz → SEBA: Bouillets source use until 2031 (interview account).
SEBA → EOS: connection-cost reimbursement (amount not specified).
Cleuson-Dixence · Appeals exchanged for a settlement
WWF → EOS / Valais: withdrawal of appeals.
EOS / Valais → environmental protection: settlement measures (amount not specified).
Nendaz · Storage and water purchases
EOS → Nendaz: storage + water supply (volume not specified).
Nendaz → EOS: water payments (amount not specified).
Navizence · Relicensing and an unsuccessful objection
Public grantors → FMG: 80-year concession, 2004–2084.
FMG → rivers: Navizence 470 L/s; Fang 50 L/s residual flows.
Gougra · Paid access for snowmaking
FMG → Zinal / Grimentz lift companies: snowmaking water (volume not specified).
Lift companies → FMG: water payments (rate not specified).
Niouc · Less water for irrigation investment
Niouc consortium → FMG: irrigation allocation cut >50% from 120 L/s.
FMG → sprinkler network: lump-sum funding (amount not specified).
Gougra · No appeal in return for restoration funding
WWF → FMG: no appeal against the Vissoie–Niouc tunnel.
FMG → Plats de la Lée: restoration funding (amount not specified).
Briey · A quantified settlement
Briey consortium → FMG: standard allocation reduced from 70 to 45 L/s.
FMG → Briey: 45 L/s; up to 70 L/s on exceptional-drought request.
Bisse Roux and St-Luc · Free quotas, paid excess
FMG → Anniviers: Roux 120,000; St-Luc 32,000 m
/year; each ≤50 L/s.
Anniviers → FMG: excess water paid at foregone kWh value (May–September use).
Cleuson and Gougra · Public parties organize for expiry
Public grantors → joint bodies: preparation for 2031 / 2039 returns.
Water quotas / payments: not yet specified.
Gougra · A price agreed now, payment due in 2039
Public grantors → FMG: CHF 15m due in 2039 (dry assets 14m + modernization 1m).
FMG → public grantors: assets at concession expiry in 2039.
Hongrin · Deferred ecological release
Vaud + Fribourg → FMHL: permission to defer the 2022 flood release.
FMHL → Hongrin: extra 2023 release = withheld 2022 volume (m
not specified).
Hongrin · Conditional snowmaking agreement
FMHL → TLML: proposed 160,000–200,000 m
/year; pumping licence required.
TLML → FMHL: payment (rate not specified); ≈80% expected return to reservoir.
Project withdrawn in 2024.
Valais · Model terms for future bargaining
Operator → municipality: reserved water free of charge (quota to be set).
Municipality → operator: extra withdrawals paid at foregone energy production cost.
Cleuson / First Dixence · Scheduled concession expiry
Alpiq → public grantors: concession expiry in 2031.
New allocation / payments: not specified.
Upper Gougra · Scheduled return and compensation
FMG → public grantors: “wet” assets free of charge + compensated assets.
Public grantors → FMG: CHF 15m agreed in 2022 (not an additional payment).
Lower Navizence · Scheduled end of the renewed term
FMG → public grantors: lower-stage concession expiry in 2084.
New allocation / payments: not specified.
Source notes and original-language excerpts
S
Andréa Savoy (July 2025). Analyse de la gouvernance de la multifonctionnalité à l’échelle des aménagements hydroélectriques : les cas de Cleuson
(Valais), de l’Hongrin-Léman (Vaud) et de la Gougra (Valais). Working paper 6, Université de Lausanne.
B
Florent Bagnoud (22 December 2022). Val d’Anniviers : on prépare déjà l’échéance de la concession des Forces motrices de la Gougra en 2039. Le
Nouvelliste.
K
Kanton Wallis / DEWK (28 February 2025). Mustervorlage Wasserrechtskonzession. Model water-rights concession; not an executed contract.
L
Bellwald. Les cabanes de gardiens de bisses. Supplied extract, PDF page 6 / printed page 139; Medard Gsponer’s retrospective account.

Reading notes: grants, transfers, entitlement confirmations and agreements are distinguished in each entry. Undated follow-on transfers are grouped with their
dated origin; their position does not establish a pre-1950 transfer. Moiry was built in 1954–1958 (S, PDF 78 / printed p. 77), so “before 1950” differs from “before
dam completion.” The 1922 purchase is outside the Gougra case and rests on a retrospective account. Evidence reflects the supplied publications, not a live status
update. “Concession” means a water-power licence where applicable; these sources do not establish a transfer of financial debt claims. The Bouillets source is
described as a sale in the narrative and as exclusive use until 2031 in an interview. The 2023 compensating release is a requirement, not verified completion.
